learning_outcomes: Explain that the cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all living organisms.
Describe Cell Theory postulated by Schleiden, Schwann, and Virchow.
Differentiate between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, and plant and animal cells.
Understand diffusion and osmosis across selectively permeable plasma membrane.
Identify functions of cell organelles: nucleus, mitochondria, plastids, endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus, lysosomes, vacuoles.
theorems_and_key_concepts: Cell Theory: All plants and animals are composed of cells; Cell is the basic unit of life; All cells arise from pre-existing cells (Omnis cellula-e-cellula).
Plasma membrane structure: Fluid mosaic model of lipids and proteins.
Mitochondria are known as the powerhouses of the cell because they synthesize ATP.
Plastids: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll for photosynthesis; Chromoplasts impart color; Leucoplasts store starch and oils.

core_concepts_and_definitions.definition: The passage of water molecules from a region of higher water concentration to a region of lower water concentration through a selectively permeable membrane.
The shrinkage or contraction of the contents of a plant cell away from the cell wall when placed in a hypertonic solution.

key_diagrams: Ultra-structure of Plant Cell vs Animal Cell
Temporary mount of onion peel cells under compound microscope

activities.title: Preparation of Temporary Stained Mount of Onion Peel
activities.title_te: ఉల్లిపొర కణాల తాత్కాలిక స్లైడ్ తయారీ మరియు పరిశీలన
activities.aim: To prepare a temporary stained mount of onion peel to observe plant cells and their nucleus under a microscope.
procedure: Take a small piece of fresh onion bulb and peel off the transparent epidermal membrane from inner concave surface using forceps.
Transfer the peel immediately into a watch glass containing water to prevent drying.
Add 1-2 drops of safranin stain to the watch glass and leave for 2 minutes.
Transfer the stained peel onto a clean glass slide with a brush and add a drop of glycerin.
Gently place a coverslip over the peel using a needle at an angle to prevent air bubbles.
Remove excess glycerin using blotting paper and observe under low and high power of microscope.
precautions: Avoid folding of the peel while placing on the glass slide.
Ensure no air bubbles are trapped under the coverslip.
activities.observations: Large number of rectangular, compactly arranged plant cells are seen. Each cell exhibits a distinct cell wall, large central vacuole, cytoplasm, and a prominent nucleus near the periphery.
activities.conclusion: The plant cell possesses a rigid cellulose cell wall and defined nucleus, confirming that the cell is the structural unit of the onion peel.

summary_points: Cells are enclosed by plasma membrane and have distinct organelles.
Plant cells differ from animal cells by possessing cell wall, plastids, and large vacuoles.

learning_outcomes: Define a tissue as a group of similar cells performing a specific function.
Classify plant tissues into meristematic (apical, intercalary, lateral) and permanent tissues (simple and complex).
Differentiate between parenchyma, collenchyma, and sclerenchyma.
Explain functions of complex permanent tissues: xylem (tracheids, vessels, xylem parenchyma, xylem fibres) and phloem (sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma, phloem fibres).
Classify animal tissues: epithelial, connective (blood, bone, cartilage, areolar, adipose), muscular (striated, unstriated, cardiac), and nervous tissue.
theorems_and_key_concepts: Meristematic tissue cells are active, have dense cytoplasm, thin cellulose walls, prominent nuclei, and lack vacuoles.
Sclerenchyma cells are dead, have thickened lignified cell walls with no internal space, providing mechanical strength.
Xylem transports water and minerals unidirectionally from roots to leaves.
Phloem translocates photosynthetic food bidirectionally between leaves and storage organs.
Neuron is the structural and functional unit of the nervous system consisting of cyton, dendrites, and axon.

core_concepts_and_definitions.definition: A cluster of cells with a common origin and similar structure that work together to perform a particular specialized function.
The developmental process of taking up a permanent shape, size, and function by cells derived from meristematic tissue.

key_diagrams: Location of apical, intercalary, and lateral meristems in plant body
Transverse sections of Parenchyma, Collenchyma, and Sclerenchyma
Neuron (nerve cell) structure showing cell body, axon, and dendrites

activities.title: Growth of Roots in Onion Bulbs (Meristematic Tissue Observation)
activities.title_te: ఉల్లిగడ్డ వేర్ల పెరుగుదల - విభాజ్య కణజాల పరిశీలన
activities.aim: To observe root tip growth and determine the effect of removing the apical meristem.
apparatus: Two glass jars filled with water
Two onion bulbs A and B
procedure: Place one onion bulb on each jar with roots dipping in water.
Measure root lengths daily for 3 days.
On day 4, cut root tips of bulb B by about 1 cm using scissors.
Continue recording root lengths in both jars for 5 more days.
precautions: Keep water level touching base of bulbs throughout.
Cut tips cleanly without crushing root tissue.
activities.observations: Roots of bulb A continue growing, while roots of bulb B stop growing after tips are removed.
activities.conclusion: Growth occurs at root tips due to apical meristem; cutting tips removes meristematic cells, halting growth.

summary_points: Plant tissues are divided into meristematic and permanent tissues.
Animal tissues comprise epithelial, connective, muscular, and nervous tissues.

learning_outcomes: Understand the basis of classification of living organisms.
Explain Whittaker's Five Kingdom Classification: Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia.
Classify Kingdom Plantae into Thallophyta, Bryophyta, Pteridophyta, Gymnosperms, and Angiosperms.
Classify Kingdom Animalia into non-chordates (Porifera to Echinodermata) and chordates (Vertebrata: Pisces, Amphibia, Reptilia, Aves, Mammalia).
Understand binomial nomenclature proposed by Carolus Linnaeus.
theorems_and_key_concepts: Classification reflects evolutionary history (phylogeny).
Binomial Nomenclature consists of two Latinized words: Genus (capitalized) and species (lowercase).
Vertebrata possess notochord, dorsal nerve cord, paired gill pouches, and coelomic body.

core_concepts_and_definitions.definition: The formal scientific system of naming organisms using two components: generic name and specific epithet.
Plants with hidden reproductive organs that do not produce seeds (Thallophytes, Bryophytes, Pteridophytes).

key_diagrams: Whittaker's Five Kingdom Classification hierarchy chart
Flowchart of Plant Kingdom classification based on body differentiation and vascular tissue

activities.title: Observation of Spirogyra under Microscope
activities.aim: To observe the filament structure and spiral chloroplasts of Spirogyra.
apparatus: Pond water sample with green filamentous algae
procedure: Collect green slimy filaments from fresh pond water.
Place 1-2 filaments on a glass slide in a drop of water.
Cover with coverslip and observe under compound microscope.
precautions: Separate the filaments gently to prevent overlapping.
activities.observations: Unbranched green cylindrical filaments with ribbon-shaped spiral chloroplasts containing pyrenoids are visible.

summary_points: Organisms are classified into five kingdoms based on cell structure and nutrition.
Animals are classified based on symmetry, germ layers, and coelom.

learning_outcomes: Distinguish between health ('a state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being') and disease.
Differentiate acute diseases from chronic diseases, and infectious from non-infectious diseases.
Identify infectious agents: viruses, bacteria, fungi, protozoans, worms.
Explain means of transmission: air-borne, water-borne, sexual, vectors.
Understand principles of prevention and treatment, and immunization.
theorems_and_key_concepts: Health is individual as well as community dependent.
Infectious diseases are caused by biological pathogens and can spread from person to person.
Principle of Immunization: Introducing weakened pathogen stimulates immune memory producing antibodies without causing severe disease.

core_concepts_and_definitions.definition: The process of developing immunity against infectious pathogens through vaccination.
An intermediate organism (such as female Anopheles mosquito) that transmits infectious pathogens from a reservoir to a host.

key_diagrams: Common modes of disease transmission flowchart (Direct and Indirect contact)
Microscopic view of common human pathogens (Bacteria, Virus, Protozoa)

activities.title: Community Health Survey on Common Infectious Diseases
activities.aim: To survey local neighborhood community for incidence of infectious diseases and analyze sanitation factors.
procedure: Survey 10 households in your neighborhood.
Record family members who suffered from diseases in the last 6 months (cold, diarrhea, malaria, dengue).
Examine neighborhood drinking water source and stagnant water drainage conditions.
Tabulate disease occurrence vs hygiene levels.
precautions: Seek consent from households before asking health survey questions.
activities.observations: Incidence of water-borne and vector-borne diseases is noticeably higher in areas with poor drainage and open garbage disposal.
activities.conclusion: Clean drinking water, vector control, and public sanitation are essential public health measures.

summary_points: Disease-free is not identical to healthy.
Prevention of disease is far more effective than cure.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Differentiate between acute and chronic diseases with one example of each.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: తీవ్రమైన (స్వల్పకాలిక) మరియు దీర్ఘకాలిక వ్యాధుల మధ్య భేదాలను ఒక్కొక్క ఉదాహరణతో రాయండి.

learning_outcomes: Understand the abiotic components of biosphere: air, water, soil.
Explain the role of atmosphere in climate control and wind formation.
Understand air, water, and soil pollution and their impacts.
Describe biogeochemical cycles: Water cycle, Nitrogen cycle, Carbon cycle, Oxygen cycle.
Explain greenhouse effect, global warming, and ozone layer depletion.
theorems_and_key_concepts: Biogeochemical cycles maintain dynamic equilibrium of nutrients in the biosphere.
Nitrogen fixation converts atmospheric N2 into usable nitrates and nitrites via Rhizobium bacteria.
Ozone layer (O3) in stratosphere protects earth from harmful solar ultraviolet radiation.

core_concepts_and_definitions.definition: The trapping of terrestrial infrared radiation by atmospheric greenhouse gases (CO2, CH4, water vapor), keeping Earth's surface warm.
The cyclic movement of essential nutrient elements through biotic and abiotic components of the biosphere.

key_diagrams: Nitrogen Cycle in Nature schematic diagram
Carbon Cycle showing photosynthesis and fossil fuel combustion

activities.title: Demonstrating Soil Erosion and Protective Role of Vegetation
activities.title_te: మృత్తికా క్రమక్షయం మరియు వృక్షసంపద రక్షణ పాత్ర ప్రదర్శన
activities.aim: To observe that vegetation cover prevents soil erosion caused by flowing water.
apparatus: Two identical wooden trays with drainage holes
procedure: Fill both trays equally with loose garden soil.
In tray A, grow grass / seedlings until green cover establishes; leave tray B bare.
Tilt both trays at equal slope into collection beakers.
Pour equal amount of water slowly using sprinkler over both trays.
Compare volume and muddiness of runoff water collected.
precautions: Pour water at identical rate and height on both trays.
activities.observations: Water collected from bare soil tray B is heavily muddy and contains eroded topsoil; runoff from tray A with vegetation is largely clear.
activities.conclusion: Plant roots bind soil particles and foliage reduces impact of raindrops, effectively preventing soil erosion.

summary_points: Nutrients cycle continuously between physical environment and living organisms.

learning_outcomes: Understand the need for increasing sustainable food production through Green Revolution and White Revolution.
Explain crop variety improvement: hybridisation, high yield, disease resistance, agronomic traits.
Explain crop production management: nutrient management (manures, fertilizers), irrigation, cropping patterns (mixed, intercropping, crop rotation).
Explain crop protection management: weed, insect pest, and disease control.
Explain animal husbandry: cattle farming, poultry farming, fish production (capture, culture, composite fish culture), and apiculture (beekeeping).
theorems_and_key_concepts: Crops require 16 essential nutrients: Air provides C and O; Water provides H; Soil supplies 13 nutrients (6 macro and 7 micro).
Composite fish culture maximizes fish yield by stocking surface feeders (Catla), column feeders (Rohu), and bottom feeders (Mrigal/Common Carp).
Intercropping and crop rotation maintain soil fertility and reduce pest infestation.

core_concepts_and_definitions.definition: Growing two or more crops simultaneously on the same field in a definite row pattern (e.g. soybean + maize).
Compost prepared using earthworms to hasten the decomposition of plant and animal waste.

key_diagrams: Composite fish culture schematic showing feeding zones

activities.title: Visit to a Local Agricultural Farm / Dairy Farm
activities.title_te: స్థానిక వ్యవసాయ క్షేత్రం / పాడి పరిశ్రమ సందర్శన
activities.aim: To observe modern animal husbandry practices in cattle management and milk production.
procedure: Visit a government or cooperative dairy farm.
Observe cattle shelter design: roof, slope of floor, ventilation, drainage.
Record breeds maintained: indigenous (Red Sindhi, Sahiwal) and exotic (Jersey, Holstein-Friesian).
Inquire about feed: roughage (fodder) vs concentrate (proteins and minerals).
Observe hygiene and vaccination schedules for prevention of diseases.
precautions: Maintain hygiene and bio-security protocols upon entering farm premises.
Do not disturb or agitate animals.
activities.observations: Cross-breeding indigenous cows with exotic breeds produces high milk-yielding animals with high disease resistance.
activities.conclusion: Proper shelter, nutritious feed, cross-breeding, and health care are essential components of scientific cattle management.

summary_points: Sustainable agriculture balances high yield with environmental preservation.
Mixed farming and composite aquaculture maximize farm productivity.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: పాడి పశువుల సంరక్షణ పద్ధతులను అధ్యయనం చేయడానికి స్థానిక డెయిరీ ఫారమ్‌ను సందర్శించే క్షేత్ర పరిశీలన విధానాన్ని వివరించండి.
